name: Atrial Fibrillation Europe
remarks: European calibration of atrial fibrillation (v2 — fixed).
CHANGES vs v1:
Bug 1 — Removed AF_Complication_Check / AF_Stroke.
stroke_europe.json already handles stroke for AF patients via
Stroke_High_Risk_Age_Check (reads atrial_fibrillation == true).
Having a second stroke source was double-counting CVA 230690007
and is the primary cause of the observed 13% stroke prevalence.
Bug 2 — Removed AF_Complication_Check infinite loop (98.5% → looped forever).
End_AF_Review now routes directly back to AF_Followup_Delay.
Added  — Alcoholism risk modifier: patients with alcoholism == true
(set by substance_use_europe_v2) have ~2× AF incidence,
consistent with ESC 2020 evidence on alcohol and AF.
USAGE NOTE:
This module REPLACES atrial_fibrillation.json (US module).
Remove atrial_fibrillation.json from the modules directory.
The US module reads atrial_fibrillation_risk (set by cardiovascular.json)
and was firing independently, adding 9-10% additional AF on top of this
module's 6-8%, together producing the observed 17% cohort prevalence.
CALIBRATION:
Lancet Reg Health Europe 2024: AF affects 1.5-2% of EU adults currently;
lifetime risk ~1 in 3-5 after age 45 (ESC Atlas 2020).
Target cohort prevalence (mean age 52.6): ~3-5%.
Age-stratified annual incidence (ESC 2020):

R4 verification round 3 (2026-08-29): rates x0.617. Measured at 4.06% against a 2.5% ESC/EHRA reference (+62%). Note this row grew between rounds 1 and 2 without being touched, because the module is risk-tiered on IHD and COPD and round 2 enlarged both of those populations.
R5 (2026-09-30): incidence refitted against Heeringa et al. 2006 (Rotterdam) table 2,
which supplies all seven age bands from 55-59 to 85+. R4 ran +41% at 60-64 rising to
+112% at 85+ because a single 75+ hazard of 0.0154 ran unbounded to age 100. The 75+
rate halves; all seven reference bands now land within 20%, median 3%.
Two things were established while fitting and belong on the record.
AF_ANNUAL_DELAY PRECEDES THE FIRST ROLL, so exposure starts at 56 and not at 55.
Ignoring that predicts the 55-59 band 38% too high. With it, the closed form
1-exp(-H) reproduces the measured run across all seven bands at a mean ratio of 1.015.
EXCESS MORTALITY IS NOT IDENTIFIABLE from a cross-sectional prevalence reference.
Fits at 0, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6% annual excess mortality all reach the same median
deviation of 3%, because a higher death rate is absorbed by a higher incidence. This
module still has no Death state, and the flat-ish top hazard stands in for the excess
mortality atrial fibrillation really carries. Adding it would need an INDEPENDENT
incidence reference to pin the pair down; calibrating it against prevalence alone
would be fitting one unknown with zero information.
AF is rare before 55; model onset from 55 onwards.
Only proceed if patient has not already been diagnosed with AF.
